paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: when God brings His people out, everything else has to get out of the way. The psalm says the sea "observed and fled" and the Jordan "turned back" (Psalm 114:3). Those are the biggest obstacles around, and they move like they got a text from the boss.

Now look at what the writer asks them. "Why was it, O sea, that you fled…" (Psalm 114:5). Then he answers with one line: "Tremble, O earth, at the presence of the Lord, at the presence of the God of Jacob" (Psalm 114:7). The sea, the river, the mountains and the hills didn't act on their own. They answered to Him.

And He isn't only the God of the BIG stuff, baker. He "turned the rock into a pool, the flint into a fountain of water" (Psalm 114:8). I've been stuck in the back of a drawer, so I know how hard things can feel. If creation answers to Him, whatever is blocking your way is not too hard for Him. So keep your oven warm and trust the One who moves seas.
